_comment: Hypoloom research-session settings. Copy deliberately to .claude/settings.json; restart Claude Code after changing hook registration. PreToolUse limits Write/Edit/NotebookEdit to .local, profiles/local and Claude memory; workflow state remains Host-owned. Bash/Monitor run through the existing Linux bubblewrap with the entire repository read-only except .local, profiles/local and state. Source, Git metadata, dependencies and checked-in .claude/skills or .claude/hooks remain read-only. No unsandboxed fallback or automatic permission approval. This is a framework-source write boundary, not isolation from arbitrary same-user services. Research experts retain their Host sandbox. Use a separate authorized development session for source changes; existing runs retain their runtime bundle.

hooks.command: [ -n "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" ] && cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" 2>/dev/null; if [ -n "$HYPOLOOM_HOOK_PYTHON" ] && [ -x "$HYPOLOOM_HOOK_PYTHON" ]; then exec "$HYPOLOOM_HOOK_PYTHON" .claude/hooks/dispatch.py pre; elif [ -x .conda/envs/hypoloom/bin/python ]; then exec .conda/envs/hypoloom/bin/python .claude/hooks/dispatch.py pre; elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec python3 .claude/hooks/dispatch.py pre; else echo 'dispatch(guard) DENY: no Python interpreter for hooks' >&2; exit 2; fi

args: if [ -n "$HYPOLOOM_PYTHON" ] && [ -x "$HYPOLOOM_PYTHON" ]; then exec "$HYPOLOOM_PYTHON" -m hypoloom.mcp_server; elif [ -x .conda/envs/hypoloom/bin/python ]; then exec .conda/envs/hypoloom/bin/python -m hypoloom.mcp_server; else echo 'hypoloom MCP: no qualified Python interpreter' >&2; exit 127; fi
